title: Enabling Large Dynamic Neural Network Training with Learning-based Memory Management
problem: Training dynamic neural networks faces memory capacity problems due to increasing model size and limited GPU memory. Tensor management in DyNNs is challenging because their dynamic structure makes memory access patterns unpredictable.
motivation: Dynamic neural networks offer high computational efficiency and strong representation capability, but memory constraints prevent training of large models on limited GPU resources.
method: DyNN-Offload employs a learned neural network (pilot model) to predict tensor memory access patterns and guide offloading decisions. The system reduces pilot model complexity by using a new DyNN representation and aggregating individual operator predictions into group operator predictions, enabling fast inference with minimal overhead while maintaining high prediction accuracy.
key_novelty: Learning-based pilot model approach to predict dynamic tensor access patterns for efficient GPU memory offloading.
contributions: DyNN-Offload system enabling 8x larger dynamic neural network training on single GPU compared to PyTorch baseline
Learned pilot model with reduced feature space and complexity for predicting tensor accesses with low inference overhead
Outperforms UVM by 3x and DTR by 2.1x in maximum batch size on AlphaFold production workload

metrics.speedup: 8x training capacity increase vs PyTorch, 3x vs UVM, 2.1x vs DTR in maximum batch size
metrics.accuracy: High pilot model inference accuracy (specific value not quantified)

primary_theme: Learning-based memory management for dynamic neural networks
